title: The Ide subgroup of Igbo
description: Where the Ide sit among the Igbo, and what distinguishes them.
html:
Ide Subgroup of Igbo

1. Defining the Purpose and Identity of Each Clan

Each clan must have a clear purpose and identity rooted in the values of Ide Igbo culture.

Clan-Level Leadership

Clan Head (Ideana na Nze): Each clan is led by Ideana na Otu Nze, chosen based on wisdom, experience, and merit. The leader of each clan’s town will be known as Aga/Duaga

Council of Elders: The Clan Head is supported by a council of elders, who provide guidance and ensure decisions align with tradition.

Igbo Influence: Use the Ozo title system to recognise and honour leaders.

Asian Influence: Adopt Confucian principles of hierarchical respect and filial piety.

Subgroup-Level Leadership

Grand Council: The subgroup is governed by a Grand Council comprising representatives from each clan, which ensures that all voices are heard.

Igbo Influence: Use the Ikalama (meeting of the minds) for meetings and where consensus-based decisions are made.

Asian Influence: Incorporate the Mandate of Heaven concept, where leaders are seen as chosen by divine will.

Ulide (Art and Culture Clan)

Purpose: Preserve and promote the creativity, artistic expression, and cultural heritage of the Ide & Igbo general.

Incorporate uli body art, mbali art installations, and storytelling traditions. Introduce calligraphy using Ndebe script, tea ceremonies, and traditional dances like Igbo chant performances.

Identity: They are the soul of the subgroup, responsible for festivals, rituals, and cultural education.

Uli body art & Mbali art:

These arts will be an integral part of Ide culture. Mbali art will be strictly used in holy temples and personal shrines. It will be modified and modernised to make it unique for Ide people. Uli art will be used for beautification, body tattoos, and art designs.

Tea Ceremony:

This tea ceremony is held during family gatherings, especially sleepovers. It is a must to be done after ikwo aka. The tea is made from hibiscus, ginger, scent leaf, or oregano. During this time, discussions and fun continue, which means it is the moment everyone comes together to gist and laugh, regardless of age.

Ulide Clan Careers:

The Art and Culture Clan has immense potential to generate income in and outside the subgroup by leveraging its creative talents and cultural heritage. Here’s a breakdown of the most lucrative opportunities, focusing on event planning, media business, music, and other ventures that can help them thrive in the modern economy:

1. Event Planning & Management

Organise cultural festivals, corporate events, and weddings.

Earn through event fees, vendor partnerships, and ticket sales.

2. Media Business

Produce films, TV shows, and digital content.

Monetise via content sales, sponsorships, and freelance services.

3. Music and Performance Arts

Record and sell music, perform at events, and offer dance workshops.

Generate income from album sales, performance fees, and classes.

4. Cultural Tourism

Offer guided tours, workshops, and cultural festivals.

Earn through tour fees, merchandise sales, and partnerships.

5. Art and Craft Business

Sell handmade crafts and custom orders, and host art exhibitions.

Monetise via product sales, commissions, and workshops.

6. Fashion and Design

Create culturally inspired clothing, accessories, and interior designs.

Earn through product sales, design services, and collaborations.

7. Publishing and Literature

Write books, magazines, and digital content about the subgroup’s culture.

Monetise via book sales, subscriptions, and sponsored content.

8. Gaming and Interactive Media

Develop culturally inspired games, VR experiences, and educational apps.

Earn through game sales, licensing, and sponsorships.

By leveraging their creativity and cultural heritage, the Art and Culture Clan can build a thriving business model that preserves traditions while generating sustainable income.

Calligraphy:

It will be the writing of Ndebe script as an art form, combining purely visual art with interpretation of the literary meaning. There will be yearly competitions for this, with huge price(oko) money, to promote the writing script as Ide's heritage.

Igbo chant performances:

This traditional Igbo chant performance, called mbem, will be a core part of the Ulide clan. It will be improved to encourage demonstrations and storytelling.

This clan controls Ndenka guild.

Ezeme (Entrepreneurship Clan)

Purpose: Drive trade, commerce, and innovation.

Use the Igba Boi apprenticeship system to train young entrepreneurs in trades. Introduce guild systems (like Chinese Hang or Japanese Za) to regulate trade and craftsmanship.

Identity: They are the economic backbone, ensuring resource distribution and wealth generation. They are to make sure every Ide clan is wealthy and insured.

Ezeme clan: This clan produces Isi Udo, Iboma, and Isi Oba. They are the king makers.

Ezeme Careers:

The Entrepreneurship Clan can drive economic growth, innovation, and sustainability within the subgroup and broader society. They can explore various opportunities by leveraging their trade, commerce, and innovation skills. Here’s a detailed look at what the Entrepreneurship Clan can do in the modern era:

1. Technology and Innovation

Launch tech startups and e-commerce platforms.

Develop digital payment systems and innovation hubs.

2. Sustainable Business Practices

Invest in renewable energy and sustainable agriculture.

Start recycling ventures and create eco-friendly products.

3. Cultural and Creative Industries

Develop cultural tourism and creative ventures like fashion, design, and media production.

4. Education and Training

The clan-owned school offers entrepreneurship workshops, mentorship programs, and vocational training. The Igba Boi apprenticeship model is the main pattern of education, but it is a modernised version.

Create online courses for skill development.

5. Financial Services

Provide microloans, grants, and investment funds via clan-owned banks.

Offer financial literacy programs and consulting services.

6. Real Estate and Infrastructure

Develop residential and commercial properties.

Invest in public utilities and transportation networks.

7. Health and Wellness

Establish healthcare facilities and telemedicine platforms.

Create wellness products and fitness centres.

8. Food and Beverage Industry

Invest in agribusiness and farm-to-table ventures.

Market traditional beverages and health-focused drinks.

9. Collaboration and Networking

Form trade associations and build international trade relationships.

Collaborate with other clans and external businesses.

10. Social Entrepreneurship

Launch social enterprises and non-profits to address community issues.

Promote corporate social responsibility (CSR) and organise fundraising events.

By focusing on these areas, the Entrepreneurship Clan can drive economic growth, innovation, and sustainability, benefiting the subgroup and the broader society.

Commercial guild organisation (Otu Nze):

A trading guild similar to the Chinese Hang or Japanese Za could be created in Nigeria and modified to fit the cultural and economic context of the Igbo people. Otu Nze is derived from Idenze and must be from the Ide tribe because they are part of its lawmakers.

One of the strongest foundations of this clan will be the“Ọmụmụ” and “Idenze” families, who will be the strongest in the clan. Omumu leads the hospitality and healthcare business, while Idenze, from the Royal Lineage of Ikala, leads the tech and real estate business. This family will come directly from the lineage of Idenze, the founder of the Ide tribe. Ọmụmụ produces the Iyi.

Oyiora (Politics and Leadership Clan)

Purpose: Crowns the Ikala, govern, mediate disputes, and represent the subgroup.

Igbo Influence: Use the Nze title system to recognise leaders and the Ofo (symbol of authority) to legitimise decisions.

Asian Influence: Adopt Confucian principles of merit-based leadership and filial piety.

Identity: They are the decision-makers, ensuring justice, order, and diplomacy. They are there to negotiate on behalf of Ide Igbo.

The leadership structure should reflect the values of both cultures, emphasising respect, merit, and community.

The Political and Leadership Clan can strategically infiltrate and influence Nigerian & international politics, particularly within the Igbo political landscape, by leveraging their expertise in governance, diplomacy, and leadership. Here’s a structured plan for how they can achieve this:

1. Building a Strong Foundation

Education and Training

Political Academies: Establish institutions to train aspiring Ide leaders in leadership, governance, and public policy.

Workshops and Seminars: Regularly organise training sessions on political strategy, public speaking, and campaign management.

Mentorship Programs

Experienced Leaders: Pair young, aspiring politicians with experienced leaders for guidance and mentorship.

Internships: Offer internships within the clan’s political offices to provide hands-on experience.

2. Grassroots Mobilisation

Community Engagement

Town Hall Meetings: Regularly hold town hall meetings to understand community needs and build trust.

Local Projects: Initiate and support community development projects to demonstrate commitment and capability.

Youth Involvement

Youth Wings: Create youth wings within the clan to engage and mobilise young people.

Scholarships and Grants: Provide educational scholarships and grants to politically active youth.

3. Strategic Alliances and Networking

Political Parties

Membership: Encourage clan members to join major political parties, particularly those with significant influence in Igbo regions.

Leadership Roles: Aim for leadership positions within these parties to influence policy and decision-making.

Coalitions and Partnerships

Alliances: Form alliances with other political groups and ethnicities to strengthen political influence.

NGOs and Civil Society: Collaborate with NGOs and civil society organisations to advocate for common goals.

4. Effective Communication and Media Strategy

Media Presence

Social Media: Utilise social media platforms to reach a broader audience and engage with constituents.

Traditional Media: Regularly appear on TV, radio, and in newspapers to discuss key issues and policies.

Public Relations

Press Releases: Issue press releases to communicate the clan’s positions and achievements.

Public Speaking: Develop strong public speaking skills to convey messages and inspire support effectively.

5. Policy Development and Advocacy

Research and Development

Think Tanks: Establish think tanks to research and develop policies that address key issues affecting the Igbo people and Nigeria at large.

Policy Papers: Publish policy papers and white papers to influence public opinion and political discourse.

Advocacy

Lobbying: Engage in lobbying efforts to influence legislation and government policies.

Public Campaigns: Launch public campaigns to advocate for specific policies or reforms.

6. Electoral Strategy

Candidate Selection

Merit-Based Selection: Choose candidates based on merit, integrity, and capability rather than nepotism or favouritism.

Diverse Representation: Ensure diverse representation to appeal to a broad spectrum of voters.

Campaign Management

Data-Driven Campaigns: Use data analytics to understand voter behaviour and tailor campaign strategies.

Grassroots Campaigning: Focus on grassroots campaigning to build a strong voter base.

Election Monitoring

Transparency: Advocate for transparent and fair electoral processes.

Monitoring: Deploy clan members to monitor elections and ensure integrity.

7. Governance and Accountability

Public Office

Effective Governance: Once in office, focus on effective governance, transparency, and accountability.

Community Feedback: Establish mechanisms for regular community feedback and responsiveness.

Anti-Corruption Measures

Zero Tolerance: Implement zero-tolerance policies for corruption within the clan and its political offices.

Transparency Initiatives: Promote transparency initiatives to build public trust.

8. Cultural and Historical Leverage

Igbo Identity

Cultural Pride: Emphasise and celebrate Igbo cultural heritage to build a strong, unified identity.

Historical Context: Use historical context to highlight the contributions of the Igbo people to Nigerian politics and advocate for equitable representation.

Unity and Solidarity

Igbo Unity: Promote unity among Igbo politicians and leaders to present a cohesive front.

Collaborative Efforts: Encourage collaborative efforts to address common challenges and goals.

9. Long-Term Vision and Sustainability

Strategic Planning

Long-Term Goals: Develop a long-term strategic plan for sustained political influence and leadership.

Succession Planning: Ensure a pipeline of future leaders through continuous training and development.

Sustainable Development

Community Development: Focus on sustainable community development projects that have long-term benefits.

Policy Continuity: Advocate for policies that ensure continuity and long-term impact.

Also, this clan cannot be the Ikala. Only Idenze family can be the Ikala.

Dilibe (Science and Health Clan)

Purpose: Advance knowledge, cure diseases, and develop technology.

Igbo Influence: Use traditional herbal medicine (ogwu) and knowledge of local plants.

Asian Influence: Incorporate practices like acupuncture, Ayurveda, and traditional Chinese medicine.

Identity: They are the innovators who improve the quality of life through research and healing.

Udeze (Military and Law Enforcement Clan)

Purpose: Protect the subgroup and maintain internal order.

Igbo Influence: The Ekpe secret society model for organised defence and justice was used to create a cult called Mbem.

Asian Influence: Adopt the discipline and strategy of samurai & Shaolin warrior traditions.

Identity: They are the protectors, ensuring safety and security.

Idenze (Priesthood and Teaching Clan)

Purpose: Provide spiritual guidance, education, and moral instruction.

Igbo Influence: Use the Dibia (priest-healer) system for spiritual leadership and divination.

Asian Influence: Incorporate Buddhist or Taoist monastic traditions for teaching and meditation.

Identity: They are the educators and spiritual guides, preserving knowledge and morality.

They're part of the clan with Ono-Idenze who can become the Ikala. Ikala is the de facto leader of Ide and like a Pope to the people practising Odiana.

Isiome (Agriculture & Tech Clan)

Purpose: Ensure food security and manage natural resources.

Igbo Influence: Use traditional farming techniques like shifting cultivation and communal labour (olu).

Asian Influence: Introduce terrace farming (common in Southeast Asia) and rice cultivation methods.

Identity: They are the nurturers, sustaining the subgroup through farming and land stewardship.

2. Establishing Leadership and Governance

The leadership structure should reflect the values of both cultures, emphasising respect, merit, and community.

Clan-Level Leadership

Clan Head (Ikaka): Each clan is led by a Clan Head, chosen based on wisdom, experience, and merit.

Council of Elders: The Clan Head is supported by a council of elders, who provide guidance and ensure decisions align with tradition.

Igbo Influence: Use the Ozo title system to recognise and honour leaders.

Asian Influence: Adopt Confucian principles of hierarchical respect and filial piety.

Subgroup-Level Leadership

Grand Council: The subgroup is governed by a Grand Council comprising representatives from each clan, which ensures that all voices are heard.

Igbo Influence: Use the Amai (meeting of the minds) system for consensus-based decision-making.

3. Spiritual and Cultural Foundations

Spirituality and culture are central to both Igbo and Asian traditions. Here’s how to blend them:

Spiritual Practices

Igbo Influence: Emphasise the role of Chi (personal god) and Ana (earth goddess) in daily life. Each clan has its shrine for ancestral veneration.

Asian Influence: Introduce ancestor veneration practices, such as offering flowers and incense at family altars. Incorporate meditation and mindfulness practices.

Cultural Practices

Festivals: Each clan has its festival, but there are also subgroup-wide celebrations. For example:

New Yam Festival: Ubi (Igbo): Celebrated by the Agriculture Clan, incorporating Asian harvest rituals.

Lantern Festival: Okuenu (Asian): Celebrated by the Art and Culture Clan, featuring Igbo dance and music.

Rituals: Blend Igbo Iko Ji (yam planting) rituals with Asian tea ceremonies to create unique cultural practices. Also, introduce the maize planting culture alongside yams and hibiscus flowers to make the celebration of Ubi unique to Ide than every other Igbo sub-group. Ubi happens on the tenth, and it also marks the birthday of the founder, while it also becomes the subgroup’s New Yam festival, and the beginning of the planting season of zobo (hibiscus flowers), which happens on the 11th of August, where families and individuals donate seeds and plants to their Ndose, who then gives them to farmers.

4. Economic and Social Systems

The economic and social systems should reflect the values of both cultures, emphasising community, skill-sharing, and sustainability.

Economic Systems

Igbo Influence: Use the Igba Boy apprenticeship system to train young people in trades and crafts.

Asian Influence: Introduce guild systems to regulate trade and ensure quality.

Social Systems

Igbo Influence: Emphasise communal living and shared labour (oru). Each town has a central meeting square (Obu) for gatherings.

Asian Influence: Incorporate Confucian values of respect for elders and family harmony.

5. Conflict Resolution and Unity

Conflict resolution should be fair, respectful, and rooted in tradition.

Conflict Resolution

Igbo Influence: Use the Igo Ofo system, where elders mediate disputes and swear on the Ofo (symbol of truth and justice).

Asian Influence: Incorporate Confucian principles of harmony and respect to prevent conflicts.

Unity

Shared Identity: Despite their differences, the clans share a common identity and work together during crises.

Grand Festival: An annual subgroup-wide festival that celebrates unity and diversity, featuring performances, rituals, and feasts from all clans.

By blending Igbo and Asian systems, the clan system becomes a rich, dynamic structure honouring tradition while fostering innovation and unity. Let me know if you’d like to explore any specific aspect further!
